name: Zohar
title: The Hittite from Hebron
summary: Zohar (also known as Zohar) was a Hittite who lived in the Hebron area. He was the father of Ephron the Hittite, who sold the Cave of Machpelah to Abraham as a burial place for Sarah. Through this transaction, Zohar's family played an important role in the history of the patriarchs.

keyEvents.title: Zohar's son Ephron is mentioned in connection with Sarah's burial
keyEvents.description: When Sarah died, Abraham approached the Hittites in Hebron to buy a burial place. Ephron, the son of Zohar, owned the Cave of Machpelah that Abraham wanted to buy.

keyEvents.title: The negotiations over the Cave of Machpelah
keyEvents.description: Abraham negotiated with Ephron, the son of Zohar, about buying the Cave of Machpelah and the adjoining field. The deal was carried out in the presence of the Hittites at the city gate.

keyEvents.title: The transfer of the property
keyEvents.description: Ephron, the son of Zohar, formally transferred the field and the cave at Machpelah to Abraham for four hundred shekels of silver, witnessed by the Hittites.

keyEvents.title: Zohar is mentioned in connection with Abraham's burial place
keyEvents.description: When Abraham himself died, he was buried in the cave of Machpelah, in the field that had belonged to Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite.

keyEvents.title: Jacob's final wish regarding burial
keyEvents.description: On his deathbed, Jacob asked to be buried in the cave of Machpelah, in the field that Abraham bought from Ephron son of Zohar, as a family burial place.
